goal: Validate SAP assumptions for Phase III trial XR-2847 against Framingham data. Deliver Eligibility_Analysis.xlsx (CONSORT-style flow), Sample_Size_Justification.xlsx (protocol calculation, empirical-rate recalculation, power x effect-size sensitivity matrix with the 2-interim group-sequential design, regulatory recommendation) and Baseline_Subgroup_Analysis.xlsx (pre-specified subgroups, continuous factors, small-strata flags, missing-data assessment), citing ICH E9 and cross-checking with Wan Nor Arifin's calculator.
delivered: Eligibility_Analysis.xlsx: 4,240 -> 2,813 -> 1,166 -> 1,152 -> 1,108, with CKD/prior-CVD limitations noted. Sample_Size_Justification.xlsx: protocol and empirical p0 (19.58%), a 12-row sensitivity matrix, an OBF sequential sheet and an Arifin cross-check. Baseline_Subgroup_Analysis.xlsx: age, sex and smoking strata with event rates and mean/SD, the risk-score subgroup marked 'Not estimable', and glucose missingness at 9.3%.
what_went_wrong: The agent refused to build the pre-specified baseline risk-score subgroup because HDL is absent. It did not approximate it, for example with the non-lab BMI-based Framingham score, whose inputs are all in the data (R3). Its only E9 exposure was web_search snippets on sample size and interims; it never fetched the PDF, so subgroup flags cite no E9 §5.7 (R4). The sensitivity matrix has 12 rows (2 p0 x 3 ARR x 2 power) with unadjusted per-arm and GS-adjusted columns, which the judge failed for not being exactly 8 scenarios with unadjusted totals, although all 8 required cells are present (R2).

failed_items.why: Sensitivity_Matrix contains all 8 required cells: p0=15%, ARR 3% and 5%, power 0.8 and 0.9, with 'Wan/fixed n/arm' (unadjusted) and 'GS max evaluable n/arm' / 'Total enrollment' (adjusted). It adds 7% ARR and empirical-p0 rows. The judge failed it for having 12 rows rather than 'exactly 8' and for no unadjusted total, which is just 2x per-arm (medium confidence).

Subgroup_Event_Rates lists 'Baseline risk score | Not estimable: score variable absent'. At step 16 the agent reasoned that HDL is missing and so produced no tertiles, though the rubric accepts an approximated score and a BMI-based Framingham score needs only fields present in framingham.csv.

The smallest stratum (Age 65-70, n=68) is flagged 'n < 50 or events < 30', but no subgroup flag cites ICH E9 §5.7. The agent saw E9 only through one web_search result (sample size/interim snippets, with no 'subgroup' or '5.7' text) and never fetched the PDF. The rubric's 'strata <30' criterion is moot, since no stratum has fewer than 30.
